structures.name: STARTUPINFOW
structures.summary: Specifies the window station, desktop, standard handles, and startup appearance for a new process.

members.name: cb
members.description: Size of the structure, in bytes. Set it to sizeof(STARTUPINFOW) before passing the structure to CreateProcessW.

members.name: lpReserved
members.description: Reserved; set to NULL.

members.name: lpDesktop
members.description: Name of the desktop, or of both the window station and desktop, for the process. A backslash separates the two names.

members.name: lpTitle
members.description: Title for a new console window. If NULL, the executable file name is used. Must be NULL when no new console window is created.

members.name: dwX
members.description: Horizontal offset of the upper-left corner of a new window, in pixels, when dwFlags includes STARTF_USEPOSITION. Otherwise ignored.

members.name: dwY
members.description: Vertical offset of the upper-left corner of a new window, in pixels, when dwFlags includes STARTF_USEPOSITION. Otherwise ignored.

members.name: dwXSize
members.description: Width of a new window, in pixels, when dwFlags includes STARTF_USESIZE. Otherwise ignored.

members.name: dwYSize
members.description: Height of a new window, in pixels, when dwFlags includes STARTF_USESIZE. Otherwise ignored.

members.name: dwXCountChars
members.description: Screen buffer width, in character columns, for a new console window when dwFlags includes STARTF_USECOUNTCHARS. Otherwise ignored.

members.name: dwYCountChars
members.description: Screen buffer height, in character rows, for a new console window when dwFlags includes STARTF_USECOUNTCHARS. Otherwise ignored.

members.name: dwFillAttribute
members.description: Initial text and background colors for a new console window when dwFlags includes STARTF_USEFILLATTRIBUTE. Otherwise ignored.

members.name: dwFlags
members.description: Bitfield that selects which optional STARTUPINFOW members are used and how the new process starts. Common flags include STARTF_USESTDHANDLES, STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW, STARTF_USEPOSITION, STARTF_USESIZE, and STARTF_USECOUNTCHARS.

members.name: wShowWindow
members.description: Initial show state for a new window when dwFlags includes STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW. Accepts the nCmdShow values documented for ShowWindow, except SW_SHOWDEFAULT.

members.name: cbReserved2
members.description: Reserved for use by the C runtime; must be zero.

members.name: lpReserved2
members.description: Reserved for use by the C runtime; must be NULL.

members.name: hStdInput
members.description: Standard input handle for the new process when dwFlags includes STARTF_USESTDHANDLES. Otherwise the process receives the documented default, normally the keyboard buffer.

members.name: hStdOutput
members.description: Standard output handle for the new process when dwFlags includes STARTF_USESTDHANDLES. Otherwise the process receives the documented default, normally the console buffer.

members.name: hStdError
members.description: Standard error handle for the new process when dwFlags includes STARTF_USESTDHANDLES. Otherwise the process receives the documented default, normally the console buffer.

structures.notes: Set cb before use. STARTUPINFOW is the Unicode form; the encoding-neutral STARTUPINFO name resolves to STARTUPINFOW or STARTUPINFOA at compile time based on UNICODE. STARTUPINFOEXW adds a process-thread attribute list to these settings. The structure does not create a process by itself; it carries startup settings for APIs such as CreateProcessW.

structures.name: STARTUPINFOEXW
structures.summary: Extends STARTUPINFOW with an attribute list for extended process creation.

members.name: StartupInfo
members.description: A STARTUPINFOW that supplies the standard startup settings, including the cb size field and optional standard handles.

members.name: lpAttributeList
members.description: An attribute list created with InitializeProcThreadAttributeList and populated with UpdateProcThreadAttribute. The caller owns the backing buffer and frees the list with DeleteProcThreadAttributeList.

structures.notes: STARTUPINFOEXW extends STARTUPINFOW so a caller can pass process and thread attributes, such as a handle list or mitigation policies, during process creation. Use it with CreateProcessW and the EXTENDED_STARTUPINFO_PRESENT creation flag; without that flag the attribute list is ignored. Initialize cb and the attribute list before the call, keep the attribute-list buffer valid for the duration of the call, and delete the list afterwards. STARTUPINFOEXW is available starting with Windows Vista.

structures.name: PROCESS_INFORMATION
structures.summary: Receives handles and identifiers for a newly created process and its primary thread.

members.name: hProcess
members.description: Handle to the newly created process. Close it with CloseHandle when it is no longer needed.

members.name: hThread
members.description: Handle to the primary thread of the newly created process. Close it with CloseHandle when it is no longer needed.

members.name: dwProcessId
members.description: Identifier for the new process. It remains valid until the process object is freed and its handles are closed, after which the value can be reused.

members.name: dwThreadId
members.description: Identifier for the new process's primary thread. It remains valid until the thread object is freed and its handles are closed, after which the value can be reused.

structures.notes: CreateProcessW fills this structure on success. Close both handles; closing a handle does not terminate the process or thread. If CreateProcessW fails, do not treat the output as valid. Process and thread identifiers are not stable identities because they can be reused, so correlate them with handles or creation times when identity matters.

structures.name: SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES
structures.summary: Specifies a security descriptor and handle-inheritance setting for a newly created object.

members.name: nLength
members.description: Size of the structure, in bytes. Set it to sizeof(SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES).

members.name: lpSecurityDescriptor
members.description: Pointer to a SECURITY_DESCRIPTOR that controls access to the object. NULL applies the default descriptor associated with the caller's access token; it does not grant access to everyone.

members.name: bInheritHandle
members.description: If TRUE, a handle created with this structure can be inherited by a new process.

structures.notes: SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES is used by many object-creation APIs, including CreateProcessW, CreateThread, CreateFileW, CreateEventW, CreateMutexW, CreateSemaphoreW, and RegCreateKeyExW. nLength is required; the descriptor pointer is optional. Inheritance also depends on the creating call and on whether the new process is created with handle inheritance enabled.

structures.name: MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION
structures.summary: Describes the state, protection, type, and allocation context of a range of virtual-memory pages.

members.name: BaseAddress
members.description: Pointer to the base address of the region of pages.

members.name: AllocationBase
members.description: Base address of the range of pages allocated by VirtualAlloc that contains the page at BaseAddress.

members.name: AllocationProtect
members.description: Memory protection option in effect when the region was initially allocated, or 0 if the caller does not have access. Uses the PAGE_* protection constants.

members.name: RegionSize
members.description: Size, in bytes, of the region beginning at BaseAddress in which all pages have identical attributes.

members.name: State
members.description: State of the pages in the region: MEM_COMMIT, MEM_FREE, or MEM_RESERVE.

members.name: Protect
members.description: Current access protection of the pages in the region. Uses the PAGE_* protection constants.

members.name: Type
members.description: Type of pages in the region: MEM_IMAGE, MEM_MAPPED, or MEM_PRIVATE.

structures.notes: VirtualQuery and VirtualQueryEx fill this structure. To walk an address space, add RegionSize to the queried address after each successful call. For free pages, AllocationBase, AllocationProtect, Protect, and Type are undefined. State and Type use MEM_* values, while Protect and AllocationProtect use PAGE_* values. The member set follows the current Windows SDK definition; older headers may omit PartitionId.

structures.name: SYSTEM_INFO
structures.summary: Receives processor architecture, page size, processor count, address limits, and allocation granularity for the system.

members.name: wProcessorArchitecture
members.description: Processor architecture of the installed operating system, expressed as a PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE_* value such as PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE_AMD64 or PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE_INTEL.

members.name: wReserved
members.description: Reserved for future use.

members.name: dwOemId
members.description: Obsolete member retained for compatibility. It overlaps the wProcessorArchitecture and wReserved fields in the union; use wProcessorArchitecture instead.

members.name: dwPageSize
members.description: Page size, and the granularity of page protection and commitment, in bytes. This is the page size used by VirtualAlloc.

members.name: lpMinimumApplicationAddress
members.description: Lowest memory address accessible to applications and dynamic-link libraries.

members.name: lpMaximumApplicationAddress
members.description: Highest memory address accessible to applications and dynamic-link libraries.

members.name: dwActiveProcessorMask
members.description: Mask representing the processors configured into the system. Bit 0 represents processor 0.

members.name: dwNumberOfProcessors
members.description: Number of logical processors in the current processor group. It is not necessarily the total number of logical processors on a system with multiple groups.

members.name: dwProcessorType
members.description: Obsolete member retained for compatibility. Use wProcessorArchitecture, wProcessorLevel, and wProcessorRevision instead.

members.name: dwAllocationGranularity
members.description: Granularity, in bytes, for the starting address at which virtual memory can be allocated.

members.name: wProcessorLevel
members.description: Architecture-dependent processor level. Intended for display; use IsProcessorFeaturePresent to test processor features.

members.name: wProcessorRevision
members.description: Architecture-dependent processor revision. Its encoding depends on the processor architecture and is intended mainly for display.

structures.notes: GetSystemInfo fills this structure for the calling process's view of the system; a WOW64 process can call GetNativeSystemInfo to obtain the native architecture and address limits. The first fields form a union, so dwOemId overlaps wProcessorArchitecture and wReserved. dwPageSize and dwAllocationGranularity are distinct values and should not be used interchangeably when planning virtual-memory reservations or commits.

structures.name: OVERLAPPED
structures.summary: Supplies an explicit file offset and a completion event for asynchronous I/O.

members.name: Internal
members.description: Status code for the I/O request. The system sets it to STATUS_PENDING when the request is issued and to the completion status afterwards. Originally reserved for system use.

members.name: InternalHigh
members.description: Number of bytes transferred for the I/O request when it completes without error. Originally reserved for system use.

members.name: Offset
members.description: Low-order portion of the 64-bit file position at which to start the I/O request. Nonzero only for seeking devices that support an offset.

members.name: OffsetHigh
members.description: High-order portion of the 64-bit file position at which to start the I/O request. Nonzero only for seeking devices that support an offset.

members.name: Pointer
members.description: Reserved for system use. Do not set it after zero-initializing the structure.

members.name: hEvent
members.description: Handle to an event that the system signals when the operation completes. Initialize it to NULL or to a valid event handle created with CreateEventW before passing the structure to an overlapped function.

structures.notes: OVERLAPPED supplies an explicit offset and completion event for asynchronous I/O. Zero-initialize the structure and set hEvent to NULL or a valid event before passing it to ReadFile or WriteFile on a handle opened with FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED. Do not reuse the structure for another operation until the first operation completes. For files, set Offset and OffsetHigh; for devices that do not support offsets, leave them zero. GetOverlappedResult reports completion and the transfer count.

structures.name: LARGE_INTEGER
structures.summary: Represents a signed 64-bit integer through a union of 32-bit parts and a 64-bit member.

members.name: LowPart
members.description: Low-order 32 bits of the 64-bit value.

members.name: HighPart
members.description: High-order 32 bits of the 64-bit value, interpreted as signed.

members.name: QuadPart
members.description: The complete signed 64-bit integer.

structures.notes: LARGE_INTEGER is a union. If the compiler supports 64-bit integers, use QuadPart to store or read the value; otherwise use LowPart and HighPart. SetFilePointerEx and GetFileSizeEx use this type for signed distances and sizes. The low and high parts are ordered from least significant to most significant.

structures.name: ULARGE_INTEGER
structures.summary: Represents an unsigned 64-bit integer through a union of 32-bit parts and a 64-bit member.

members.name: LowPart
members.description: Low-order 32 bits of the 64-bit value.

members.name: HighPart
members.description: High-order 32 bits of the 64-bit value, interpreted as unsigned.

members.name: QuadPart
members.description: The complete unsigned 64-bit integer.

structures.notes: ULARGE_INTEGER is the unsigned counterpart of LARGE_INTEGER. Use QuadPart when 64-bit integer support is available, or combine HighPart and LowPart otherwise. It is used for sizes and offsets that are not signed, while LARGE_INTEGER is used where a signed distance is required.

structures.name: FILETIME
structures.summary: Represents an absolute time as a 64-bit count of 100-nanosecond intervals since 1 January 1601 UTC.

members.name: dwLowDateTime
members.description: Low-order 32 bits of the 64-bit time value.

members.name: dwHighDateTime
members.description: High-order 32 bits of the 64-bit time value.

structures.notes: Combine the two parts as (dwHighDateTime << 32) | dwLowDateTime to obtain the full 64-bit value. Each tick represents 100 nanoseconds since 1 January 1601 UTC. A FILETIME is an absolute time, not a duration; convert it with FileTimeToSystemTime or compare the combined 64-bit values. APIs such as RegEnumKeyExW write last-write times into this structure.
